column1: # What a user types into the app, checked through the whole app without a screen (keyboard hook → controller →
# simulated text box and Korean IME). Every reported case goes here.
#   mode      EN or KO, the IME mode while typing
#   typed     the keys, words separated by spaces; Hangul stands for the keys that type it (KO 내 = so).
#             A space is typed at the end, or Enter when it ends in ⏎, or nothing more when it ends in .
#   expected  what the text box shows, without that last space or Enter, or = for exactly what was typed
# ID protection is off by default (Settings.ProtectIds): a name-like single word + Enter converts too
# mirrored: the same shapes typed in the other mode
# Korean mode, proper syllables and an English part of four letters or less: kept as typed (해미면 is not goal면)
# Korean mode keeps 초4가 (a 4th grader); ch4 is English-mode only
# Shift only slips on past a key that needs it, in a long word: not dkssUD, not RK는
# ...but Shift let go inside a syllable is a slip even at the start (the s is the 받침 of 쓴)
# 2026-10-13: English mode, an abbreviation without vowels + 가
# 2026-10-13: English mode, a particle typed after a space
# Long text: possessives, a quote before a word, two-letter capitalized words (all typed in Korean mode)
# Fuzz edge cases: hashtags, mentions, times, emails, URLs and code names in the wrong mode
# Long text: to between numbers in Korean mode; a capital + group syllable + particles
# Dotted abbreviations typed in Korean mode
# Fuzz edge cases, round 2 (Korean mode): Www, camelCase, snake_case with a syllable, mentions, a.m. after context
# Fuzz round 3 (Korean mode): chat abbreviations inside English, vowel pieces in snake_case, camelCase in syllables
# Possessives: English mode keeps them, Korean mode restores short ones
# snake_case with a short consonant piece; chat pieces alone stay
# A number does not end the sentence context (Korean mode, English sentence)
# Fuzz seeds 21-22: rare listed words stay whole, a camelCase part that is a word is not split
# Fuzz round 5 (Korean mode): an ordinal th at the start of a sentence; a common word over a capital + Korean
# Fuzz seeds 23-24: a word typed with Shift for ㄲ stays Korean; camelCase right after the capital; mixed vowels are keys
# 2026-10-13: English mode, a number + a word + ending
# 2026-10-13: English mode, a capital + particle over a rare word
# 2026-10-14: a symbol written before a word
# Fuzz seed 100: a name on the list + particle is not a shorter word + a longer ending
# 2026-10-14: the word before, in quotes, follows the next word (look-back)
